160+ hours played I honestly think Cursed Companions is one of the most underrated co-op games out there. The game is built around communication. You defeat monsters by speaking the correct phrases, everyone gets cursed words they must avoid saying, and many mechanics depend on what your team says. It creates some of the funniest and most chaotic moments I've had in a multiplayer game. There's plenty of content: three Acts with different bosses, Challenge Mode, Endless Mode for those who enjoy pushing themselves, and Traitor Mode (up to 16 players), which gives strong Among Us vibes. Normal runs support up to 8 players, and that's where the game shines. Solo is still fun for achievement hunting, but playing with friends is a completely different experience. One of the biggest reasons I've spent over 160 hours here is the developers. They're incredibly active, respond quickly, fix bugs, and genuinely listen to community feedback. The official Discord is also great for reporting issues, suggesting features, getting achievement help, or simply finding teammates. The game isn't perfect. Since maps are procedurally generated, you'll occasionally find a bug, and voice recognition can be tricky if English isn't your first language (I have a strong Slavic accent myself). However, both problems have workarounds, and the developers improve the game constantly. If public lobbies seem empty, don't assume the game is dead. Many people play in private groups, and the Discord is the easiest place to find others. You can also play across regions without noticeable lag. I'm not even a horror game fan, but this game got me into the genre. There are monsters and tension, but it isn't filled with cheap jump scares, making it a great entry point for players like me. This is a small indie game made by a passionate team, and it has huge potential. At full price it's already worth it, and with the current 30% discount, it's an easy recommendation. Bring a few friends, give it a chance, and don't let this hidden gem disappear.

Cursed Companions is a cooperative horror adventure that turns one of the most ordinary aspects of multiplayer gaming into its defining feature. Developed and published by Crimson Forge Studios, the game revolves around voice communication, but with a clever twist that constantly keeps players on edge. Every participant is assigned a secret cursed word, and speaking it causes damage, making even the simplest conversations risky. This unique mechanic transforms routine teamwork into a constant balancing act where every sentence must be carefully considered. Rather than relying solely on jump scares or combat to create suspense, the game generates tension through player interaction, making every session feel unpredictable and full of memorable moments. The game's procedurally generated dungeons provide a strong foundation for replayability, ensuring that each expedition presents new environments, layouts, and dangers. Exploration is more than simply searching for treasure or avoiding monsters, as players must use their voices to activate spells, illuminate dark corridors, disable traps, solve environmental puzzles, and support teammates. At the same time, careless speech can trigger hidden threats or accidentally injure allies, forcing everyone to communicate creatively under pressure. This innovative blend of voice recognition and cooperative gameplay encourages teams to develop unconventional strategies while creating plenty of humorous situations that naturally emerge from the game's unusual rules. One of the game's greatest strengths lies in its diverse selection of supernatural enemies. Instead of following familiar horror game formulas, many creatures react differently depending on what players say or how they behave. Certain monsters may respond to profanity, while others are influenced by specific phrases or verbal interactions, requiring players to learn each enemy's quirks through experimentation. This design keeps encounters engaging because defeating threats often depends as much on communication as it does on skill. A variety of magical items and equipment further expands tactical possibilities, giving players tools for offense, defense, mobility, and support while complementing the game's emphasis on teamwork. Beyond its standard cooperative dungeon runs, Cursed Companions includes multiple gameplay modes that add even more variety. Boss battles introduce larger-scale challenges that demand coordination, while Endless Mode pushes players to survive increasingly difficult encounters for as long as possible. The addition of Traitor Mode brings an entertaining social deduction element, allowing one or more players to secretly work against the group while pretending to cooperate. Combined with emergency discussions and player voting, these mechanics create entertaining scenarios where deception and suspicion become just as important as survival. Unlockable cosmetics, achievements, and home customization systems provide meaningful progression that encourages players to continue exploring everything the game has to offer. The visual presentation embraces a stylized art direction that blends spooky environments with a lighthearted sense of humor, allowing frightening moments and comedic situations to coexist naturally. The atmosphere benefits greatly from the game's sound design, as voice recognition is central to nearly every mechanic. When everything works smoothly, speaking commands and reacting naturally with friends creates an immersive experience unlike most cooperative horror games. However, the heavy dependence on microphones and accurate speech recognition also means that technical inconsistencies or communication issues can occasionally interrupt the flow of gameplay. These limitations are understandable given the ambitious concept, but they remain factors players should consider before jumping in. Cursed Companions stands out because it fully commits to an original gameplay idea and builds every aspect of its design around it. By making communication both the players' greatest strength and their biggest weakness, it delivers an experience that constantly produces laughter, tension, and unexpected stories. Its combination of procedural exploration, creative monster mechanics, varied game modes, and cooperative problem-solving gives it excellent replay value for groups looking for something different from traditional horror titles. Although its reliance on voice recognition may not appeal to everyone, those willing to embrace its unconventional design will find a remarkably inventive multiplayer experience that rewards teamwork, quick thinking, and adaptability. Rating: 8/10

Funny game that keeps you giggling and laughing while you play with your friends or strangers. I recently Purchased this game because of my kid. We played it easily for hours having fun and laughing and giggling at all the stilly phrases as people are running around asking for someone to tell them "I still love you" even though they are cursed. And all the fun little things in the game. I found that its really fun. I haven't run into any major bugs, But one of our team members ended up in a small "room" It could be considered maybe two blocks wide. I was successful on my roll and got to join him in this little room, finding out he had been in there for over 11 minutes already. I had added time earlier so we had around 7 mins or so left and we couldn't get out and we just stayed in there giggling about it dancing and doing other things. One even logged out and in to see if they could summon us out and nope. we ended up losing but we loved every moment. We made the best out of it. and Why not it didn't keep us from playing to me it seemed like a fantastic trap for one person to get stuck in that needed summoned to get out. And no one knows that's going on except dead ones. Though I didn't realize he was stuck in a room until after I spawned on him. LOL then our other member joined us. SO ya, tons of silliness to have here. As for the empty public areas, some like me still do that. I have too many discords to connected unless I get to the point I have to report a BUG. I will be avoiding that, But if you see me in the public ones feel free to join in for the giggles!
